To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LCN2 overexpression in aged mice induces adipose tissue hypertrophy with a shift in the expression of genes involved with adipogenesis and inflammation and leads to impaired glucose metabolism and altered liver function, suggesting a role in metabolic disorders and ageing.
systemic lipocalin- 2 (LCN-2) overexpression in aged mice leads to increased adipose tissue mass, altered glucose metabolism, and liver involvement.
LCN2 profoundly impacts adipocyte size and glucose metabolism and should be considered as risk factor in ageing and metabolic disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of systemic overexpression of lipocalin 2 on adipose tissue in aged transgenic mice.
the effects of lipocalin 2 overexpression on glucose metabolism in a mouse model of ageing.
the role of LCN2 in ageing, and it provides a model to study the effects of LCN2 on glucose homeostasis and adipose tissue function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LCN2 is a risk factor for metabolic disorders in ageing, which is a relevant aspect in the light of the increasing number of ageing people in the world.
LCN2-TG mice are a model of ageing and metabolic disorders.
LCN2 overproduction in aged animals is a risk factor for metabolic disorders and obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LCN2 over-expression is associated with increased adipocyte size and altered expression of several genes involved in adipogenesis and inflammation.
LCN2 overexpressing mice display increased adiposity, altered glucose metabolism, and increased liver damage.
LCN2 overexpressing mice have increased adiposity, decreased glucose tolerance and impaired insulin sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LCN2 is a risk factor for obesity in the elderly and that its overexpression may contribute to a vicious circle in which the metabolic syndrome and obesity are mutually reinforcing.
LCN2 overexpressing mice are smaller and have increased visceral adipose tissue, which is associated with increased cell size and inflammation, and impaired glucose tolerance.
systemic LCN2 upregulation in ageing is associated with a reduced glucose tolerance, which may be due to an impaired insulin secretion and/or insulin sensitivity.
